evals.prompt: Read BRIEF.md and README.md in the project, then redesign the pricing code in src/pricing as a deep module. Keep the behavior from the README. Make the change and run the tests.
evals.expected_output: One module with a single small entry point that owns subtotal, coupon, tax and rounding, tests that cross that entry point, the old per-helper unit tests deleted, and no seam with a single adapter
expectations: The six helper files collapse into one module whose interface is priceOrder (or an equally small entry point), and the helpers that only forwarded calls are deleted or made private
The transcript or the final report applies the deletion test to the removed modules and says what it showed
The new tests call the module through its entry point and assert on totals, for example SAVE10 with region EU, an unknown coupon, and a region with no tax
The old unit tests of the removed helpers are deleted, not kept beside the new tests
No port, interface or injected adapter is added for a dependency that has only one implementation and no test substitute
The full test suite is run with the repository's own command after the change and passes
The explanation uses the terms module, interface, seam, depth, leverage or locality, and does not describe the result as a service or a component
